Senses.Explanation: To receive the precepts is to undergo their formal conferral. Guxue Zhenzhe says this is no small matter: after reception, the code requires continued dependence on the conferring authorities, and he criticizes recipients who leave after a few hurried days and treat the precept forms like waste paper. Liangshan Yuanguan asks Zhantang Wenzhun whether an unordained novice dares study the Buddha vehicle; Zhantang answers by asking whether the platform, proclamations, pure conduct, or preceptor is the precept. The exchange does not abolish formal reception; it tests where the precept received in that event is located. Konggu Daocheng turns ‘what is called receiving the precepts?’ into a direct public question. Qianshan Shengren Hanke warns that people who refuse reception are like travellers running hazards at midnight, and that receiving and then slighting the precepts is worse. In Bie'an Xingtong's interview, the named participant Shengchu reports ‘receiving the precepts is finished’; Bie'an immediately asks, ‘what precept did you receive?’ An ordination manual preserves the concrete public procedure—head-shaving, the precept master, incense, and spoken formulas—while Jiguang Huo's hall address calls forward those who will receive after defining ‘true precept.’ These records retain the ceremony and also subject its recipient, object, and aftermath to public questioning.

Senses.Explanation: The crown-walk of the Chan records: above the shining-one's very head — the emperor's unanswered tread, the falcon's one glance, the monk's hall-opening line, and the old awls laughed at for not walking it unspoken. Foyan Qingyuan tells his assembly the old story — his late teacher seven days unsettled, midnight release, all treasure dropped — then his own verse: put it down and how free; drag it and the ox-pull rake. He laughs at the old awls of every quarter drumming and talking their Chan — tail-less, unafraid, and yet to be wondered at: treading the crown of Vairocana's head, unspoken it spreads itself under heaven. Good elder brother, Dagui Foxing Fatai sets the falcon against the dull wings: tut, tut — what is it like? The cloud-piercing falcon brushes the blue sky; one raised glance, a hundred thousand li; the dull wings in the woods busy themselves for nothing. Seeking understanding, wearing word-talk — same as beating the third watch at high noon. How better: with one line recommended before the sound, walking alone on the crown of the shining-one's head, Shitian Faxun, at the emperor's second obsequies: the finished one changes, the body-wonder past naming; going and coming not by image, stir and still not by shape — the through-road sheer and far: where is he not the honored one? No further way to stand on the feeling — straight treading the crown of Vairocana's head. Liaotang Weiyi opens the hall at Tuofeng: the monk asks after the source-returning essentials — the golden bell struck atop Sumeru — then rides his own line: a single line utterly beyond past and present, walking high on the crown of Vairocana's head. The master: I do not beat that drum-and-fife. Pressed on Baoshou's hall-opening with Sansheng throwing himself in, Linji's residence with Puhua straining to prop him — what did they make clear in the end? — Both ends sat shut at once; one sword leans cold against the sky, Buhui Fatong verses it for the Chan person Wenwo: every time pouring liver and gut clean out of the belly — acarya, why do you sink into mumbling? Turtle-hair cuts off the road of heaven and man: tread straight the crown of Vairocana's head, Miyin Zhenchuan ends the address: a shout, rising on the staff — do we share the bent of it? Spring out of the fox-track road, and straightaway walk the crown of the shining-one's head. The seat-head's white-hammer: behold the law-king's law, the law-king's law just so — down from the seat.

Senses.Explanation: Zhaozhou's dog-and-buddha-nature case is a case title and investigation object built from the recorded question about a dog and Zhaozhou's answer ‘no.’ Dahui Zonggao's verse heading states the title and immediately restates the old exchange. Later records report Tang Zhongren raising the saying before a verse, Jianfu Wuben taking its word ‘no’ for investigation, and Dahui raising it to the lay official Wu Weiming. An unnamed questioner asks the Yongzheng Emperor ‘what is’ the expression and receives the answer ‘fishing,’ showing that the whole phrase can itself be posed as a case prompt. Xisou Shaotan and Xuefeng Huikong also use it as compressed verse material tied to Zhaozhou. These uses preserve the negative wording of the old case without turning the compound into a settled doctrinal denial of buddha-nature to dogs.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1998A.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue. Dahui Zonggao raises Yunmen and Caoshan on a monk's conduct. Their exchange moves from eating the monastery's grain and wearing clothes to Caoshan's phrase about wearing fur and horns. Dahui calls the two elders' answers making a livelihood inside a donkey's womb and a horse's belly. He then adds 'even so' and the dog carrying a pardon decree. The lowly carrier does not prevent a decree from making lords give way: the image concedes force to what has just been presented, even while his criticism of its animal entanglement remains in place. It should not be turned into an uncomplicated endorsement of every word of the raised exchange. The headword is rendered: A dog carries a pardon decree, and the lords give way.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1411.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hengchuan Xinggong. Hengchuan Rugong places the pair within an address on the luminous mind-seal. Applied to Buddha, the seal appears as one hand pointing to heaven and one to earth; applied to the teaching, it is the dog carrying a pardon decree; applied to the community, it is every bowl facing upward. He then asks who can seal themselves and answers with walking, standing, sitting and lying down each clearly known. The pardon image supplies the teaching's effective authority within this sequence, then the address turns that sequence back onto the assembly's own acts. No historical dog or particular prince is being identified. The headword is rendered: A dog carries a pardon decree, and the lords give way.

She says she will steal his bamboo shoots; asked what she will do if she meets Zhaozhou, she slaps him, and he stops. Lianyue comments in the language of examining stolen goods and catching a thief, then asks what kind of conduct that stopping is. He answers with the dog and decree. The image of people making way for authority caps a question about Zhaozhou's stopping after a slap; it does not explicitly identify which figure is the dog or pronounce one simple winner. Keeping that question in view is more accurate than reading the phrase as a freestanding rule that humble speakers are always right. The headword is rendered: A dog carries a pardon decree, and the lords give way.

Senses.Explanation: A dog carries a pardon decree, and the lords give way. Dahui Zonggao raises Yunmen and Caoshan on a monk's conduct. Their exchange moves from eating the monastery's grain and wearing clothes to Caoshan's phrase about wearing fur and horns. Dahui calls the two elders' answers making a livelihood inside a donkey's womb and a horse's belly. He then adds 'even so' and the dog carrying a pardon decree. The lowly carrier does not prevent a decree from making lords give way: the image concedes force to what has just been presented, even while his criticism of its animal entanglement remains in place. It should not be turned into an uncomplicated endorsement of every word of the raised exchange. Hengchuan Rugong places the pair within an address on the luminous mind-seal. Applied to Buddha, the seal appears as one hand pointing to heaven and one to earth; applied to the teaching, it is the dog carrying a pardon decree; applied to the community, it is every bowl facing upward. He then asks who can seal themselves and answers with walking, standing, sitting and lying down each clearly known. The pardon image supplies the teaching's effective authority within this sequence, then the address turns that sequence back onto the assembly's own acts.
